findings.issue: The English defensibly reads the genitive and its governing noun continuously, but the intervening printed full stop is not disclosed. The draft discusses the comparable punctuation in καὶ.Δίκην, while leaving this feature unmentioned and source_issues empty. This is a disclosure issue concerning the verified selected print, not evidence of an OCR error or missing wording.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a nonblocking editorial-punctuation entry quoting Γανυμήδους.ἁρπαγῇ exactly. Explain that the supplied print separates the possessor from ‘abduction’ with a full stop, whereas the English follows their grammatical relationship. Preserve the supplied Greek; label any proposed repunctuation as a proposal rather than the supplied reading. No lacuna, restoration, or additional print verification is required.

findings.source_quote: καὶ τῶν σοφῶν οἱ περιβόητοι οὐχ ἡδονὴν προκρίνουσιν καὶ αἷς ἐβουλήθησαν ἐμίγησαν;
findings.english_quote: Do not even the celebrated wise men prefer pleasure and have relations with whichever women they wished?
findings.issue: The Greek combines present προκρίνουσιν with aorist ἐβουλήθησαν and ἐμίγησαν. The draft preserves the past ‘wished’ but places ‘have relations’ under the present auxiliary ‘Do not’, obscuring the contrast between present preference and the reported past sexual conduct.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose for fresh review: ‘Do not even the celebrated wise men prefer pleasure, and did they not have relations with whichever women they wished?’ This preserves both the rhetorical negation and the source’s tense contrast.

findings.source_quote: οὐκ Ἀρίστιππος μυρισθεὶς ὅλον αὐτὸν Ἀφροδίτῃ χαρίζεται;
findings.english_quote: Does not Aristippus, perfumed all over, give himself to Aphrodite?
findings.issue: The draft attaches ὅλον αὐτὸν to μυρισθείς, effectively as an accusative of respect, yielding ‘perfumed all over’. A material alternative attaches it to χαρίζεται: after being perfumed, Aristippus gives his whole self to Aphrodite. The present rendering is defensible, but neither this attachment decision nor the alternative emphasis is disclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare the draft explicitly with ‘Does not Aristippus, after being perfumed, give his whole self to Aphrodite?’ Record both attachments and the contextual reason for choosing one. If retaining the draft, explain why ὅλον αὐτὸν is understood with the perfuming rather than as the object of χαρίζεται. Any changed main text requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἵνα γνώριμον τοῖς συνετοῖς γένηται ἵνα ᾧ ἂν τις μιγῇ, ὡς ἑαυτῷ μίγνυται
findings.english_quote: so that intelligent people may recognize that, with whomever someone has relations, he has relations as with himself
findings.issue: The supplied text repeats ἵνα. The draft renders the second occurrence as the content marker ‘that’, but its notes do not disclose or explain this construction. Reading the second clause loosely as an explanation of what becomes known is contextually defensible; treating it as another purpose clause is a material alternative. The verified wording must not silently be treated as though it contained ὅτι instead.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note identifying both occurrences of ἵνα. Explain that the draft construes the second clause as the content of the intended recognition, while an alternative retains the repeated purposive force, ‘so that … so that …’. Preserve the uncertainty over their relationship and state that no Greek emendation has been supplied. Classify this as disclosed syntactic uncertainty, not an unverified transcription defect.

findings.source_quote: τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ ἐξ ὧν σοι γράψας ὑπέμνησα συνεῖσα ἔπεχε, μήποτε ἐραστήν σου λυπήσῃς
findings.english_quote: For the rest, understand what I have reminded you of in writing, and take care never to distress a lover of yours.
findings.issue: The draft makes the written reminders the direct object of ‘understand’. In the Greek, ἐξ ὧν identifies those reminders as the basis from which understanding is obtained. On the straightforward object attachment, τὰ λοιπά is what she is to understand from them: the remaining implications. Even if τὰ λοιπά is taken adverbially as ‘for the rest’, the relationship expressed by ἐξ must remain.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose for fresh review: ‘Having understood the rest from what I have reminded you of in writing, take care never to distress a lover of yours.’ If choosing the adverbial attachment of τὰ λοιπά instead, retain an explicit ‘from’ or ‘on the basis of’ relationship rather than making the reminders themselves the object of understanding.
